:::{#exm-indset-in-np}
#### Independent set is in NP

For an input $x$ to [INDSET](#def-indset),
a certificate is the independent set itself,
written as $m$ binary digits that mark which vertices it holds.
Since $m$ is fixed by the length of the adjacency matrix in $x$,
the certificate's length depends only on $|x|$, as @def-class-np requires.
The verifier checks that $k$ digits are $1$
and that no two marked vertices are adjacent.
That takes $O(m^2)$ lookups in the adjacency matrix,
which is polynomial in $|x|$,
so INDSET is in NP (@def-class-np).
No polynomial-time algorithm that decides INDSET is known.
@arora2009computational [section 2.1] use the same example.

:::
